<Rep. Maxine Waters, Rep. Al Green, Rep. Bill Foster, Rep. Joyce Beatty, Rep. Rashida Tlaib, Rep. Sylvia R. Garcia, Rep. Nikema Williams>: H.R. 6550 requires the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (``Fed''), Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (``OCC''), Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (``FDIC''), and National Credit Union Administration (``NCUA'') to include unusually extensive information about their interactions with global financial regulatory or supervisory forums like the Basel Committee or the Network for Greening the Financial System.
There are a number of international organizations that U.S. financial regulators participate in--like the Financial Stability Board (``FSB'') and Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (``BCBS'')--that furthers our national interest by advancing policies that benefit the U.S. and allow us to monitor and shape related developments in other countries. In fact, global coordination in standard setting helps ensure financial companies don't migrate to jurisdictions with weaker standards, raising transmission risk concerns to the U.S. to the extent these entities engage in, or are otherwise connected to, cross-border financial activities.
Some of this international work touches on climate-related risks. In December 2017, several central banks and financial regulators established the Network of Central Banks and Supervisors for Greening the Financial System (``NGFS'').\1\ NGFS is a voluntary, global coordinating body intended to promote sharing of best practices regarding climate risk management for the financial sector and mobilize financing options to support the transition to a sustainable economy.\2\ NGFS issues various reports and makes non-binding recommendations aligned with the organization's purpose. In November 2021 when the United Nations convened the Climate Change Conference (``COP26''), NGFS released the ``Glasgow Declaration,'' outlining various steps the group would take to meet the objectives of the Paris Agreement, including with respect to developing climate scenarios for testing purposes, providing further analysis to integrate climate change considerations into monetary policymaking, and addressing data gaps that hinder monitoring and mitigation of climate-related risks.\3\ After U.S. agencies served on the NGFS for several years, Trump's regulators withdrew our agencies from the organization.
\1\NGFS, Origin and Purpose (accessed on Jul. 7, 2023).
\2\NGFS, Origin and Purpose (accessed on Jul. 7, 2023).
\3\NGFS, The NGFS publishes the ``NGFS Glasgow Declaration'' and continues to foster climate action by central banks and supervisors (Nov. 3, 2021).
Americans for Financial Reform is opposed to H.R. 6550. Moreover, while Republicans seek to enhance oversight of regulators participating in these international forums, they have done nothing to hold Trump's Treasury Department accountable for offering a $40 billion bailout to Argentina or to learn anything about the terms and conditions of that support. Nevertheless, the unusually-extensive reporting requirements of this bill would chill efforts to promote international coordination of regulatory standards, which help ensure there is not a global race to the bottom to the jurisdiction with the weakest standards, and the work that can be done on matters that require international coordination like addressing climate-related financial risks. Committee Republicans passed a similar bill with even more extensive provisions last Congress (H.R. 4823, 118th) on a party-line vote.
For these reasons, we oppose H.R. 6550.
Sincerely,
Maxine Waters,
Ranking Member.
Al Green,
Bill Foster,
Joyce Beatty,
Rashida Tlaib,
Sylvia R. Garcia,
